summary: Web-based log application for a 28ft box truck with separate admin and user logs; users can upload documents and submit questions, and admins can view/manage uploads and questions.
imageRequirements:
## Required Images
- Minimal monochrome line-art illustration of a 28ft box truck, front 3/4 view, clean vector style (truck-logo.dim_512x512.png)

existing_features.title: Implement Internet Identity authentication and role-based access so the app supports two roles: Admin and User. Users can access their own log entries, uploads, and questions; Admins can access all users’ logs, uploaded documents, and questions.

Create a truck log feature for a 28ft box truck where signed-in users can create, view, edit, and delete their own log entries with at minimum: date/time, optional title, notes, and an optional numeric field (e.g., mileage/odometer). Admins can view all users’ log entries.

Add document upload for users: users can upload documents (store file bytes + metadata such as filename, content type, size, upload timestamp) and view/download their own uploads. Admins can view/download all users’ uploaded documents.

Add a questions feature: users can submit questions (text + timestamp) and view their own submitted questions. Admins can view questions from all users and manage them by setting a simple status (e.g., Open/Answered) and optionally adding an admin reply.

Provide an Admin dashboard (“admin log”) and a User dashboard (“users log”) with navigation between: Truck Logs, Documents, and Questions. The Admin dashboard must include overviews and lists for all users’ data; the User dashboard must show only the signed-in user’s data.

Define a consistent, distinctive visual theme for the app (colors, typography, spacing, and component styling) appropriate for a “fleet/truck operations log” product, and apply it consistently across dashboards, tables/lists, and forms (avoid a blue/purple theme).
Add the required generated image asset(s) to the frontend as static files under frontend/public/assets/generated and use them in the UI (e.g., app header/login screen).

Allow users to upload documents; admin can view uploaded documents
